items.title: Compiler memory usage/GC
items.author: Jochen
items.content:
While looking at the compiler, I noticed that has a boolean flag in the middle of its properties, that costs 8 bytes because of padding. Moving to the beginning would fit it into the padding after the type ID.

However, testing that with compiling the compiler lead to a smaller heap, and the GC doing more collections, thus adding runtime. Which lead me to look a bit into the GC. It may be that there are some phases where GC takes up time and is not very effective (not freeing a lot). Maybe fiddling with the initial heap size, and turning off GC in some phases would speed things up a bit?

Question is, is that something I put time into? Any interest in PRs in this area?

items.title: Anyone here using a bottle washer for baby bottles at home?
items.author: davidmoore
items.content: I’m a Crystal user, but this is off-topic, so bear with me. We’re expecting our first baby in a few months, and our kitchen in Columbus is small, so counter space is tight. My partner and I are trying to decide whether a dedicated bottle washer is worth it versus just hand-washing and boiling. My main concern is how well these machines actually clean the small parts, like nipples and valves, and whether they’re hard to keep clean themselves. I’ve seen some listings online but I don’t have any hands-on experience with them. If you’ve used one with an infant, was it a real time-saver or did it just add another appliance to manage? I’d also like to know if the cleaning results held up after a few months of daily use. Any input appreciated.

items.title: Invading other forums
items.author: renich
items.content:
Hey community, here’s a guerrilla marketing idea for ya ;D

Crystal punches way above its weight, yet outside our bubble almost nobody sees what we’re building with it. What if we organized a loose “Crystal out in the wild” effort?

Instead of waiting for people to stumble onto Crystal, we could actively publish more real-world writeups, problem-solving posts, benchmarks, and migration stories on broader dev spaces like HN, Lobsters, dev.to, and programming subreddits; show we actually solve problems in Crystal.

No spam or brigading; just a crew helping each other workshop drafts, stress-test benchmarks, and consistently put solid Crystal engineering in front of the wider dev world. One blog post a quarter is easy to miss; a steady stream from the community isn’t.

Would anyone be up for coordinating something like that?
